To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in patients with newly-diagnosed type 2 diabetes, self-monitoring of blood glucose has no effect on HbA1C levels, body mass index, use of oral glucose lowering drugs, or the incidence of hypoglyaemia.
self monitoring of blood sugar levels in patients with newly-diagnosed type 2 diabetes has no effect on glycemic control, but is associated with a higher score on a depression subscore.

self monitoring of bloodglucose in people with newly diagnosed diabetes had no effect on glycosylated haemoglobin levels, body mass index, the use of hypoglycemic medication, or the incidence of hypogylcemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of self monitoring of glucose in people with type 2 diabetes, particularly the effect it has on their psychological state.
the use of blood glucose monitoring by patients with diabetes, and the effect of this monitoring on glycaemic and psychological indices.
the role of self monitoring of glycaemia in the management of type 2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study do not support the widespread use of self monitoring of plasma glucose in people with diabetes.
there is no evidence to support the routine prescription of SMBG in patients with type 2 diabetes.

self-monitoring of blood glucose in newly diagnosed patients with type 2 diabetes has no effect on HbA1C and BMI, is associated with a 5-6% higher score for the depression subscale, and is associated with increased use of oral hypolycemics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self monitoring of blood sugar is not helpful for patients with type 2 diabetes.
self monitoring of blood sugar levels is not helpful for patients with type 2 diabetes.

self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) is not recommended for patients with type 2 diabetes, and that SMBG should be discouraged for patients with type I diabetes, unless they have hypoglycemic unawareness.

SMBG does not improve HbA1C levels in people with type 2 diabetes and that SMBG does increase depression scores in people with type-2 diabetes.
